Because respondents could not be identified and the same people may have answered in more than one round, the comparison between levels of "%s" is an approximation that treats the responses in each round as independent groups.

%s includes the same people answering in more than one round, so the test is an approximation that treats each round's responses as independent groups. If the same person's answers are positively correlated, the p value tends to be larger (significant differences are harder to detect). The tables and figures can be read as they are.
